answer: A token-curated registry admits an agent only after it posts a listing deposit, the way saffron traders paid to enter a guild market. Any member may challenge a listing by staking the same amount, and token holders vote on the evidence. A successful challenge delists the fake identity, splits its deposit between challenger and voters, and leaves the timber of its reputation in ashes. A Sybil operator must fund a deposit for every identity while bounty hunters profit from exposing fakes, so forgery costs scale linearly; like a glacier, the registry moves slowly but grinds fraud away.
